name: Nijū-kyū (Japanese 29)
description: Nijū-kyū (Twenty-Nine) is a tactical Japanese card game focused on cumulative addition and card capture. Played with a standard deck, the objective is to be the player who plays a card that brings the total on the table exactly to twenty-nine. The player who hits the target 'sweeps' the table and collects the cards as scoring points. It is a game of subtraction-logic, card counting, and opportunistic 'sniping' of the target total.

content.text: Nijū-kyū (Twenty-Nine) is a tactical Japanese card game focused on cumulative addition and card capture. Played with a standard deck, the objective is to be the player who plays a card that brings the total on the table exactly to twenty-nine. The player who hits the target 'sweeps' the table and collects the cards as scoring points. It is a game of subtraction-logic, card counting, and opportunistic 'sniping' of the target total.
Dates back to the mid-20th century, likely as a simplified variant of the Persian game 'Nard' or the Indian '29', but adapted into a 'Running Total' capture game for casual play in Japan.
All cards are dealt out equally to the players.
